candidates.name: Tanakaya
candidates.reason: solid, locally-noted wariko soba specialist directly across from the shrine's main entrance, but draws regular weekday queues at the busiest address in town — a backbone pick, not an off-the-beaten-path find

candidates.name: Heiwa Soba Honten
candidates.reason: popular with locals, ~10 min walk from the shrine with its own parking, but also draws frequent lines — keep as a backup, not the lead pick

candidates.name: Kizuki
candidates.reason: stone-mills its own domestic buckwheat and hand-makes noodles daily; only a single local-editorial source found within budget (no second independent corroboration), so held at shortlisted rather than shipped

candidates.name: Kawakyo
candidates.reason: counter-only, ~8-10 seats total, booked roughly a month ahead — seating the full party of 8 as a group dinner would take over the entire counter, which isn't confirmed as normal practice; too much friction for the anchor group meal

candidates.name: Nekkoya
candidates.reason: sister restaurant to Konekkoya with an exact-fit, fully private 8-person room — a strong alternative if the group wants total separation, but its menu is general Shimane izakaya fare rather than the lake-view Shinjiko-shichimi theme that fits the food priority better

candidates.name: Yamaichi
candidates.reason: rejected: has private rooms (個室あり) and serves Lake Shinji specialties, but its maximum private-room party size for a group of 8 could not be confirmed from an official source within this pass, while Konekkoya's capacity is confirmed

candidates.name: Yuushien Garden
candidates.reason: not a substitute for Adachi's borrowed-scenery 'living painting' design philosophy — Yuushien is a peony/seasonal-event garden (illuminations, flower displays), a genuinely different genre; good on its own terms, not a like-for-like swap

candidates.name: Oki Islands Day Trip
candidates.reason: physically possible as a day trip (~70 min each way via the Rainbow Jet high-speed boat), but it consumes a full day of a 4-day, culture/food-priority trip and leans nature/geopark rather than culture/history; the operator's own guidance confirms rough-weather sailings can be rerouted or cancelled, a real stranding risk for a mobility-constrained group of 8 with no slack day built into the itinerary

candidates.name: Tsuwano
candidates.reason: genuine culture + food day-trip option (preserved castle town, uzumemeshi), but Matsue + Izumo + Iwami Ginzan already fill a 4-day itinerary tightly — flagged for reconcile to weigh against the other bases rather than decided here

evidence.claim: Kamiarizuki (the shrine's lunar-calendar 'month when the gods are present') and the Kamiari-sai rites have fallen entirely within November-December in recent years (2025: Nov 20-Dec 19, per the official Izumo Tourism Association). No official 2026 dates were posted as of this research, but the pattern makes an overlap with the Oct 20-23 trip window very unlikely -- this trip does NOT land in the crowded 'gods gathering' season, contrary to a common assumption about visiting Izumo Taisha in October.

Matsue Castle's busiest hours run roughly 10am-3pm (tour buses and day-trippers cluster then, with the donjon staircase congested); arriving in early morning (8:30-9:30) or from ~4:30pm is noticeably calmer.

Peak autumn foliage color at Matsue Castle's Johzan Park typically runs mid-to-late November -- after the Oct 20-23 trip window, so the trip lands in a shoulder period, before both the koyo crowds and Kamiarizuki.

The 'Matsue Lake Line' loop bus runs about every 30 min (full loop ~50 min), Y250/ride or Y700 all-day pass, and covers Matsue Station, Matsue Castle, the Horikawa boat dock, Shiomi Nawate, and Matsue Shinjiko Onsen -- avoids long walks between the day's stops for the 2 low-mobility travelers.

Shiomi Nawate is a ~500m preserved samurai-residence street protected as Matsue's 'traditional beauty district' since 1973, reachable by a 15-min bus from JR Matsue Station -- a walkable, low-key counterpoint to the castle itself.

Tanabe Museum of Art sits inside Shiomi Nawate, adjacent to the Lafcadio Hearn Old Residence, entered through an unassuming long-gate -- a lower-profile setting than the castle or the main tourist street, despite being on the same block.
Reported hours 9:00-17:00, Y700 adult admission, closed Mondays -- sourced only from a secondary reference, not fetched from the museum's own hours page in this pass. Reconfirm before relying on it.
Kizuki, about 3 minutes' walk from Izumo Taisha's main torii, stone-mills its own domestic buckwheat and hand-makes noodles fresh daily.
Tanakaya, directly across from Izumo Taisha's main entrance, is a locally popular tri-colored wariko-soba specialist that regularly draws weekday queues.
Heiwa Soba Honten, about a 10-minute walk from Izumo Taisha with its own parking, is a popular locally-loved shop known for frequent lines even on weekdays.

Kawakyo seats only at a counter, with no tables -- multiple independent diner/guide accounts describe an 8-10 seat counter that is typically booked out roughly a month ahead, making an 8-person group booking impractical as a single party.

Konekkoya (at the Shinjiko Shijimi-kan, 2F) has a private space seating up to 24 and serves Lake Shinji shijimi and other Shimane specialties -- a party of 8 fits comfortably, and it is on-theme for the Shinjiko-shichimi food priority (lake view, shijimi-focused menu).

Nekkoya (Isemiya-cho) has a completely private room (kanzen kojitsu) seating exactly up to 8 -- an exact-fit alternative if the group wants total separation, though its menu is general Shimane izakaya fare rather than the lake-view shichimi specialty.
Adachi Museum of Art is calmest right at the 9:00 opening; tour-bus arrivals build within about an hour, with crowding particularly around 10am and again around 1pm.

Yuushien (Daikonshima) is a ~40,000 sqm pond-style landscape garden, not an Adachi-style 'living painting' -- its identity centers on seasonal event programming (peony displays, summer mist, the region's largest autumn/winter illumination); open 9:30-17:00 (last entry 16:30), Y1,000-1,800 adult.

Cars/taxis reach only the Iwami Ginzan Park visitor center; beyond that it is a ~45-min walk one-way to the Ryugenji mine shaft, or a rental e-bike (Y700/2hr) from Daikansho Plaza, or a 6-seat 'Ginzan Cart' (Y500 one-way to the mine). The cart is the only officially confirmed mobility workaround for the 2 low-walking-tolerance travelers, and one cart does not cover a party of 8 in a single trip.

Local bus service (Ishimi Kotsu) from JR Ota-shi Station to Omori/Iwami Ginzan runs on limited frequency -- the operator's own traffic-info page and multiple secondary sources advise checking the round-trip timetable in advance and allowing at least half a day for the site; a taxi stand at Ota-shi Station (Fuji Daiichi Kotsu) is the fallback if a bus is missed. Exact daily bus count could not be confirmed from a live timetable within this pass.
Crossing the Shimane mainland <-> Oki (Saigo) takes ~1 hour by the Rainbow Jet high-speed boat or ~2.5 hours by the regular ferry; a day trip is physically possible via the high-speed boat.

Oki Kisen's own guidance states that in bad weather, departure/arrival locations may change or ports may become inaccessible; the high-speed boat requires seatbelts and the operator recommends seasickness medication in advance. A cancelled or rerouted last sailing has no same-day alternative back to the mainland.

Shimane Prefecture's own transport page frames stable year-round ferry operation as an ongoing goal rather than a guarantee, without disclosing concrete cancellation-rate figures -- consistent with the operator's own weather caveat.

Uzumemeshi -- rice with vegetables, tofu, seafood and wasabi 'buried' beneath it -- is Tsuwano's signature local dish, counted among Japan's 'five great meshi,' still served as everyday local fare rather than a tourist-only novelty.

reservations.partyRules: Confirmed private space seats up to 24; a party of 8 fits comfortably. Exact release window / how-far-ahead-to-book not confirmed in this pass.
reservations.alternatives: Nekkoya (sister restaurant, Isemiya-cho) has an exact-fit fully private 8-seat room if the group wants total separation, though its menu is general Shimane izakaya fare, not lake-view shichimi. Yamaichi has private rooms but capacity for 8 is unconfirmed.

reservations.releaseWindow: roughly 1 month ahead recommended for this counter-only, popular spot
reservations.partyRules: Counter-only seating, ~8-10 seats total -- booking the full party of 8 would take over the entire counter, which is not confirmed as standard practice.

leads.claim: Some visitor reports suggest the whole counter can be reserved out for a private group by special arrangement with the owners

reservations.alternatives: Konekkoya (confirmed room up to 24, shijimi/Shinjiko theme) for the full group; Kawakyo works well for a smaller subset (2-4) wanting the counter experience.

transport.route: JR Ota-shi Station -> Omori / Iwami Ginzan (Ishimi Kotsu local bus, Omori Line)
transport.doorToDoor: JR Ota-shi Station (reachable via the San-in Main Line, ~40 min from Izumo-shi) -> local bus to Omori/World Heritage Center, then walking, e-bike, or the Ginzan Cart into the townscape and mine area.
transport.transferReality: Local bus service on the Omori Line is described by the operator and multiple secondary sources as limited; the operator's own traffic-info page directs visitors to the timetable and recommends allowing at least half a day. Exact daily frequency was not confirmed from a live timetable in this pass -- an honest gap, not an invented number.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: Cars/taxis reach only the visitor center; the mine shaft itself is a ~45-min walk beyond that. For the 2 low-walking-tolerance travelers, the 6-seat Ginzan Cart (Y500 one-way) or a rental e-bike are the only officially confirmed workarounds -- one cart does not cover a party of 8 in a single run, so the group would split across at least two cart trips or a mixed walk/cart arrangement (not itself confirmed by the operator).
transport.buffer: Official guidance recommends allowing at least half a day for the site.
transport.missedConnection: Not confirmed from a live timetable in this pass -- treat published bus times as needing an in-trip check.
transport.fallback: Taxi stand at JR Ota-shi Station (Fuji Daiichi Kotsu), confirmed via the official traffic-info page, as a paid fallback if the return bus is missed.

transport.route: Matsue (via connecting bus to Shichirui port) -> Saigo, Oki Islands, round trip
transport.doorToDoor: Connecting bus from Matsue Station to Shichirui port, then the Rainbow Jet high-speed boat (~1hr) or the larger ferry (~2.5hr) to Saigo.
transport.transferReality: The operator's own guidance states that in bad weather, departure/arrival locations may change or ports may become inaccessible -- a real risk given the trip falls in late-October's tail end of typhoon/autumn-storm season.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: The high-speed boat requires seatbelts during transit and the operator recommends seasickness medication in advance -- not ideal footing for the 2 low-mobility travelers in a swell; the larger, slower ferry is the gentler option if crossing at all.
transport.missedConnection: A cancelled or rerouted return sailing has no same-day alternative -- an unplanned overnight on the islands is the practical consequence.
transport.lastPracticalReturn: Not confirmed for a specific date in this pass -- check the operator's live timetable close to travel.
transport.fallback: None beyond an unplanned overnight on Oki; no bridge or alternative crossing exists.

saturation.note: Covered both ranked priorities (culture/history, food) plus the fragile-transport requirement across ~16 evaluated candidates. Later searches (additional soba shops, additional Matsue izakaya, a third Iwami Ginzan bus-timetable attempt) returned the same handful of domains and no new serious options. Remaining gaps -- exact Iwami Ginzan bus frequency, exact 2026 Kamiarizuki dates, Tanabe Museum's own hours page -- are all honestly flagged rather than guessed, and none is likely to flip which candidates are worth shipping: the qualitative picture (limited-but-workable bus service, trip dates fall before both Kamiarizuki and koyo season, Tanabe's hours are probably right but unconfirmed) is stable across independent sources.
